prompt: Six friends each pay $\$3.75$ for a movie ticket. How much do they pay altogether?
hint: Every friend pays the same amount. Which operation combines six equal amounts quickly?

hints.text: Every friend pays the same amount. Which operation combines six equal amounts quickly?
Work out $3.75 \times 6$. Multiply $375 \times 6$ as whole numbers first, then put two decimal places in the product.
$375 \times 6 = 2250$, which becomes $22.50$, so the friends pay $\$22.50$ altogether.

explanation: Six equal prices can be combined by multiplying the price by six: $3.75 \times 6$.
Multiply without the decimal point first: $375 \times 6 = 2{,}250$.
The price $3.75$ has two decimal places, so the product needs two as well: $22.50$.
Altogether the six friends pay $22.50$ dollars for their tickets.
